name: org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter-py
description: Machai Ghostwriter Python wrapper and command-line package, distributed on PyPI as mgw and built alongside the Maven artifact org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter-py:1.4.3. It bundles the Ghostwriter Java runtime JAR and provides a lazy JPype bridge, so Python applications and command-line users can invoke Ghostwriter without manually assembling a classpath. The public gw function forwards Ghostwriter CLI arguments; gdp scans a project for guidance tags and returns its report as a Python list; adw executes a named Act or Act expression and returns processor results as a Python list. The wrapper requires Python 3.10 or newer in practice, despite the package's declared Python >=3.9 metadata, because it evaluates PEP 604 union annotations at import time. JVM startup requires JAVA_HOME pointing to a valid JDK and JPype-compatible JVM. gdp and adw can optionally resolve extra local JAR paths or Maven coordinates through jgo. Java-side provider and model configuration is supplied using Ghostwriter's supported properties configuration or environment settings.

usageContext: Windows, Linux, and macOS command-line usage with a supported JDK
Automated guidance scanning of project files
Execution of Ghostwriter Acts against a project
Bundled Java runtime invoked from Python through JPype

features.name: gw
features.description: Runs the bundled org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.Ghostwriter entry point through JPype. The supplied argument list is forwarded to Java without Python-side option parsing; None forwards the current process arguments excluding the executable. It starts the JVM lazily and requires JAVA_HOME to identify an existing JDK when no JVM is already running. The return value is the Java entry point result, converted by JPype when it is a Java string.

examples.description: Import the public API, ask the bundled Ghostwriter CLI to display its help, and print its result. Configure JAVA_HOME before this first call so JPype can start the JVM.

features.name: gdp
features.signature: builtins.list[builtins.str] mgw.gdp(builtins.str | None model = None, builtins.str | None project_dir = None, builtins.str path = ".", builtins.str config_file = "gw.properties", builtins.str | None instructions = None, builtins.int | None threads = None, builtins.list[builtins.str] | None excludes = None, builtins.bool non_recursive = False, builtins.int | None module_thread_timeout_minutes = None, builtins.list[builtins.str] | None libs = None)
features.description: Constructs and configures the Java GuidanceProcessor, scans the selected project path synchronously, and converts its report container to a Python list. project_dir defaults to the current working directory, while path is passed to the Java scanner as a relative path or supported matcher. Optional settings provide model selection, configuration, instructions, concurrency, exclusions, non-recursive scanning, module timeout, and additional local JARs or Maven coordinates. Processing can modify matching project files; configure the Ghostwriter model/provider through supported configuration before scanning.

examples.snippet:
import mgw

report = mgw.gdp(project_dir=".", path="src", threads=2)
for entry in report:
    print(entry)
examples.description: Scan the src tree of the current project for guidance tags with two processing threads and print each report item. Set JAVA_HOME and the required Ghostwriter provider/model configuration before invoking the processor.

features.name: adw
features.signature: builtins.list[builtins.str] mgw.adw(builtins.str act, builtins.str | None model = None, builtins.str | None project_dir = None, builtins.str path = ".", builtins.str config_file = "gw.properties", builtins.str | None acts_location = None, builtins.bool interactive = False, builtins.bool disable_normal_order = False, builtins.list[builtins.str] | None libs = None)
features.description: Constructs and configures the Java ActProcessor, selects the supplied Act name or expression, scans the project path synchronously, and returns processor results as a Python list. The Java implementation handles Act loading and expression syntax. Use interactive=False for unattended execution. Optional libraries may be local JAR paths or Maven coordinates and are resolved with jgo. Configure JAVA_HOME and Ghostwriter provider/model properties before processing.

examples.snippet:
import mgw

results = mgw.adw("my-act", project_dir=".", path="src", interactive=False)
for result in results:
    print(result)
examples.description: Run an Act named my-act against the src tree of the current project in non-interactive mode, then display every result. Replace the sample Act name with an available Act and ensure its configuration and required credentials are available to Ghostwriter.

customizations.name: Ghostwriter properties configuration
customizations.description: Configure the Java Ghostwriter processor's provider, model, and other supported settings using its properties configuration or supported environment settings. The Python wrapper passes config_file to PropertiesConfigurator and leaves configuration interpretation to Java.

examples.snippet:
import mgw

report = mgw.gdp(project_dir=".", path="src", config_file="gw.properties")
examples.description: Select a project properties file when scanning. Populate it with valid settings expected by the Ghostwriter Java configuration and configure JAVA_HOME in the process environment.

examples.name: Install and run the mgw command on Windows Command Prompt
steps: Install Python 3.10 or newer and a supported JDK (the project targets Java 17).
Set JAVA_HOME to the JDK installation directory and add its bin directory to PATH.
Install the PyPI package with python -m pip install mgw; this installs the jpype1 and jgo Python dependencies.
Run mgw --help or python -m mgw --help to invoke the bundled Ghostwriter CLI.
examples.snippet:
set "JAVA_HOME=C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17"
set "PATH=%JAVA_HOME%\bin;%PATH%
python -m pip install mgw
mgw --help
examples.description: Practical Windows Command Prompt installation and invocation. JAVA_HOME must point to an existing JDK, not merely be omitted in favor of a system Java installation. For project processing, additionally configure the Ghostwriter provider/model and credentials in the supported properties configuration or environment settings.

examples.name: Build and locally install from the repository
steps: Install Maven, a compatible JDK, Python 3.10 or newer, and the Python build frontend.
From the repository root, run mvn clean package -Prelease to assemble the Java runtime and Python distributions.
Install the built Python package from src/main/python and configure JAVA_HOME before invoking it.
examples.snippet:
python -m pip install --upgrade build
mvn clean package -Prelease
python -m pip install .\src\main\python
mgw --help
examples.description: Builds the Java runtime bundled in the Python distribution and installs the local package on Windows Command Prompt. The Maven release profile assembles src/main/python/mgw/jars/ghostwriter.jar and invokes the Python build frontend.
